results.title: Credible Intervals (CI) • bayestestR
results.content: As the Bayesian inference returns a **distribution** of possible effect values (the posterior), the credible interval is just the range containing a particular percentage of probable values. For instance, the 95% credible interval is simply the central portion of the posterior distribution that contains 95% of the values. ## Different types of CIs. The reader might notice that `bayestestR` provides **two methods** to compute credible intervals, the **Highest Density Interval (HDI)** (`hdi()`) and the **Equal-tailed Interval (ETI)** (`eti()`). library(bayestestR) library(bayestestR)library(ggplot2) library(ggplot2) # Generate a normal distribution # Generate a normal distributionposterior <- distribution_normal(1000) posterior<- distribution_normal(1000) # Compute HDI and ETI # Compute HDI and ETIci_hdi <- ci(posterior, method = "HDI") ci_hdi<- ci(posterior = "HDI")ci_eti <- ci(posterior, method = "ETI") ci_eti<- ci(posterior = "ETI") # Plot the distribution and add the limits of the two CIs # Plot the distribution and add the limits of the two CIsout <- estimate_density(posterior, extend = TRUE) out<- estimate_density(posterior = TRUE)ggplot(out, aes(x = x, y = y)) + ggplot(out aes(= x = y)) + geom_area(fill = "orange") + geom_area(= "orange") + theme_classic() + theme_classic() + # HDI in blue # HDI in blue geom_vline(xintercept = ci_hdi$CI_low, color = "royalblue", linewidth = 3) + geom_vline(= ci_hdi $ CI_low = "royalblue" = 3) + geom_vline(xintercept = ci_hdi$CI_high, color = "royalblue", linewidth = 3) + geom_vline(= ci_hdi $ CI_high = "royalblue" = 3) + # Quantile in red # Quantile in red geom_vline(xintercept = ci_eti$CI_low, color = "red", linewidth = 1) + geom_vline(= ci_eti $ CI_low = "red" = 1) + geom_vline(xintercept = ci_eti$CI_high, color = "red", linewidth = 1) geom_vline(= ci_eti $ CI_high = "red" = 1). In symmetric distributions, the two methods of computing credible intervals, the ETI and the HDI, return similar results. Unlike the HDI and the ETI, which look at the posterior distribution, the **Support Interval (SI)** provides information regarding the change in the credibility of values from the prior to the posterior - in other words, it indicates which values of a parameter have gained support by the observed data by some factor greater or equal to *k* (Wagenmakers, Gronau, Dablander, & Etz, 2018).
